source_verification_receipts.verified_claim: Under Assumptions 1–3, initial distributions, transition kernels, and type probabilities are identified up to a common latent-type permutation from four consecutive observations.
Quantifier elimination is presented as a route to implicit observable constraints, model comparison, identification, and bounds in hidden-variable statistical models.
The article reduces discrete causal problems to polynomial programs and uses branch-and-bound/dual relaxation to give sharp or guaranteed non-sharp ranges and epsilon-sharpness guarantees.
The paper constructs confidence regions for identified sets and their known-function images, with pointwise and uniform asymptotic validity under stated conditions.
The paper studies partial identification of finite mixtures with observable variation in mixture weights that leaves component distributions unchanged.
